situation.problem_text:
Topic: The Pulse of Rhythm: An Introduction to Music and Measure Theory

Target audience: Middle school students or introductory music theory learners

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite: The Concept of a Steady Pulse

Lecture lines:
Music starts with a steady, recurring pulse.
Think of a heartbeat, always consistent.
These pulses provide our musical foundation.

Planned animations:
Create a glowing dot in the center of the screen (#00FF00) to represent the 'Beat'.
Animate the dot pulsing in size (scale up and down) every 1 second to emulate a heartbeat.
Fade in a label below the dot reading 'Pulse' in white (#FFFFFF) to establish the conceptual tool.

Section: section_2 — The Bar Line: Organizing the Chaos

Lecture lines:
We group pulses into equal measures.
Vertical bar lines mark the separation.
These help organize rhythmic flow clearly.

Planned animations:
Render 12 dots arranged in a horizontal row (#FFFFFF).
Animate a vertical line (#FF0000) drawing itself after every 4th dot to create the 'Bar Line'.
Animate the groups of 4 dots shifting slightly to define the 'Measures' clearly.

Section: section_3 — Time Signature: The Mathematical Blueprint

Lecture lines:
Time signatures act as our blueprint.
The top number sets beats per measure.
The bottom defines the beat's value.
Together they guide the rhythmic structure.
Imagine a chef filling musical bowls.

Planned animations:
Render a bowl shape (#FFFF00) as the 'Measure'.
Animate 4 distinct musical notes falling into the bowl one by one.
Animate a vertical wall appearing at the end of the 4th note to seal the bowl.
Add a label '4/4' above the bowl in cyan (#00FFFF) to represent the Time Signature.
Flash the label '4/4' three times to emphasize its role as the mathematical blueprint.

Section: section_4 — Visualizing Fractions in Time

Lecture lines:
Notes are like fractions of time.
Whole notes fill the entire measure.
Smaller notes divide the circle equally.
They sum perfectly to one measure.
Each wedge completes our musical clock.

Planned animations:
Render a circular clock (#FFFFFF) as a 'Whole Note' placeholder.
Animate two semi-circular wedges (#FF00FF) appearing to fill the clock face.
Animate the wedges fading into labels '1/2' in white to visualize the fractions.
Change the circle color to gradient red to green to show it filling over time.
Trigger a flash effect when the clock is full to indicate 'Measure Complete'.

Section: section_5 — Application: The Marching Ants

Lecture lines:
Marching ants show rhythm in action.
Every fourth ant wears a cap.
This accent creates a predictable structure.
The measure theory brings music order.
Rhythm is simply math in motion.

Planned animations:
Render 8 ants in a line, moving left to right across the screen (#FFA500).
Animate every 4th ant appearing with a blue cap (#0000FF) as they walk.
Animate the capped ants flashing brighter to emphasize the first beat accent.

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite: The Concept of a Steady Pulse

Lecture lines:
Music starts with a steady, recurring pulse.
Think of a heartbeat, always consistent.
These pulses provide our musical foundation.

Planned animations:
Create a glowing dot in the center of the screen (#00FF00) to represent the 'Beat'. (Wait 4s)
Animate [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/heart.svg] pulsing in size (scale up and down) every 1 second to emulate a heartbeat. (Wait 4s)
Fade in a label below the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/heart.svg] reading 'Pulse' in white (#FFFFFF) to establish the conceptual tool. (Wait 4s)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Music starts with a steady, recurring pulse.",
            "Think of a heartbeat, always consistent.",
            "These pulses provide our musical foundation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Concept of a Steady Pulse", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        pulse_dot = Dot(color="#00FF00", radius=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(pulse_dot, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        pulse_label = Text("Pulse", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(pulse_label, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        pulse_label.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        # Pulse animation using ValueTracker
        tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)
        pulse_dot.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_width(0.6 * tracker.get_value()))
        
        self.add(pulse_dot, pulse_label)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Start rhythmic pulse
        for _ in range(3):
            tracker.set_value(1.5)
            self.wait(0.3)
            tracker.set_value(1.0)
            self.wait(0.7)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(3)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Marching ants show rhythm in action.",
            "Every fourth ant wears a cap.",
            "This accent creates a predictable structure.",
            "The measure theory brings music order.",
            "Rhythm is simply math in motion."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Marching Ants", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1: Marching ants ===
        ants = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FFA500") for _ in range(8)])
        for i, ant in enumerate(ants):
            self.place_at_grid(ant, f"D{i%6+1}") # Simplified layout for movement
            ant.shift(LEFT * 4 + RIGHT * (i * 0.5))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFA500"), run_time=1)
        self.play(*[FadeIn(ant) for ant in ants], run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2: Every fourth ant wears a cap ===
        caps = VGroup()
        for i in range(3, 8, 4):
            cap = Triangle(color="#0000FF", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.1)
            cap.next_to(ants[i], UP, buff=0.05)
            caps.add(cap)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#0000FF"), *[FadeIn(cap) for cap in caps], run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3: This accent creates a predictable structure ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), *[Flash(cap.get_center(), color="#FFFFFF", flash_radius=0.2) for cap in caps], run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4: The measure theory brings music order ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5: Rhythm is simply math in motion ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)
